text:
Charle-Edouard D'Astous took the long way. Never drafted, he went from the Quebec league to the SHL with Brynas before Tampa Bay signed him, and at 28 he's suddenly one of the hottest defensemen in the league: 10 points in his last ten games, including his first three-point NHL game against Minnesota.

Our numbers say the run is mostly earned. His ice time is up almost five minutes a night over that stretch, he's quarterbacking a power play that's given him six of his 11 points, and his own chances are up too. Evolving-Hockey liked his play-driving last season, 86th percentile among defensemen once teammates and competition are accounted for.

Two caveats. He's shooting 12.5%, about double a normal rate for a defenseman, and the Lightning's five-on-five share is a bit lower with him on the ice than without him this season. Neither ruins the story. Our range has him around 43 points, which for a player who wasn't on most fans' radar in October would be a real find. Fantasy players noticed already; he's been a waiver-wire pickup all month.
headline: Charle-Edouard D'Astous is earning everything he gets
